speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you mentioned weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to begin our investigation, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of diabetes, alcohol use, and steroid use, have you noticed any numbness or tingling in your hand that started in the fingertips and moved up your arm? Additionally, do you experience any muscle cramps or weakness in your lower extremities?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) and Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP).
REQUEST TEST: Nerve Conduction Study (NCS) and Electromyography (EMG) of the right upper extremity.
DIAGNOSIS READY: Parsonage-Turner Syndrome (Neuralgic Amyotrophy) likely secondary to chronic alcohol and steroid use, given the acute onset of severe pain followed by progressive weakness and sensory loss in a single upper limb.
